podcast.title: "Pedestrian" Musical Tastes
podcast.body: Eric Burden and John Steele characterized Alan Price's musical preferences as "pedestrian" compared to their own "hippotastes" for R&B, blues, and jazz, often describing him as a "lounge player." "Both burden and steel regarded Price's tastes as rather pedestrian, when compared to their own hippotastes, saying he always regarded himself as something of a lounge player"

podcast.title: Solo Career Success
podcast.body: Following his departure from The Animals, Alan Price achieved considerable solo success. He introduced Randy Newman's songs to a broader audience and developed a jazz-influenced R&B style reminiscent of Mose Allison. "Price would go on to make many great solo records, introducing the songs of Randy Newman to a wider audience, and performing in a jazz-influenced R&B style, very similar to Moe's Allison."
